AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER

 

THIS AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of May 12, 2026 (the “Agreement Date”), by and among BROOKFIELD BANCSHARES, INC., a Delaware corporation (“Purchaser”), BRKD Merger Sub Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Merger Sub”), and NSTS BANCORP, INC., a Delaware corporation (the “Company”).

 

RECITALS

 

A.         The boards of directors of the Company and Purchaser have determined that it is in the best interests of their respective companies and stockholders to consummate the Contemplated Transactions as provided for herein, pursuant to which the Merger Sub will, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, merge with and into the Company (the “Merger”), with the Company as the surviving entity in the Merger (sometimes referred to in such capacity as the “Surviving Entity”).

 

B.         Immediately following the Merger, the Company will, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, merge with and into Purchaser (the “Holding Company Merger”), with Purchaser as the surviving entity in the Holding Company Merger.

 

C.         As an inducement to Purchaser to enter into this Agreement, concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, the directors and executive officers of the Company and the Bank have entered into a Voting and Support Agreement in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (the “Company Voting Agreement”).

 

D.         As an inducement to Purchaser to enter into this Agreement, concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, the directors and executive officers of the Company and the Bank have entered into a Confidentiality and Non-Solicitation Agreement in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit B.

 

E.         The parties desire to make certain representations, warranties and agreements in connection with the Merger and the other Contemplated Transactions, and the parties also agree to certain prescribed conditions to the Merger and other transactions.

 

AGREEMENTS

 

In consideration of the foregoing premises, which are incorporated herein by this reference, and the mutual promises, covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, the parties hereto hereby agree as follows:

 

ARTICLE 1

DEFINITIONS

 

Section 1.1      Definitions. The following terms, when used herein, shall have the following meanings.

 

(a)      “Accounting Standards” shall mean GAAP, as applied on a basis consistent with past practices and as modified by applicable regulatory accounting principles.

 

 
 
 

(b)      “Acquisition Proposal” shall mean a tender or exchange offer to acquire more than 25% of the voting power in the Company or the Bank, a proposal for a merger, consolidation or other business combination involving the Company or the Bank or any other proposal or offer to acquire in any manner more than 25% of the voting power in, or more than 25% of the business, assets or deposits of, the Company or the Bank, other than the Contemplated Transactions.

 

(c)      “Affiliate” shall mean with respect to:

 

(i)    a particular individual: (A) each other member of such individual’s Family; (B) any Person that is directly or indirectly controlled by such individual or one or more members of such individual’s Family; (C) any Person in which such individual or members of such individual’s Family hold (individually or in the aggregate) a Material Interest; and (D) any Person with respect to which such individual or one or more members of such individual’s Family serves as a director, officer, partner, executor or trustee (or in a similar capacity); and

 

(ii)    a specified Person other than an individual: any Person that directly or indirectly controls, is directly or indirectly controlled by, or is directly or indirectly under common control with such specified Person; any Person that holds a Material Interest in such specified Person; each Person that serves as a director, officer, partner, executor or trustee of such specified Person (or in a similar capacity); any Person in which such specified Person holds a Material Interest; any Person with respect to which such specified Person serves as a general partner or a trustee (or in a similar capacity); and any Affiliate of any individual described in clauses (B) or (C) of this subsection (ii).

 

(d)      “Benefit Plan” shall mean each of the following plans, agreements, and arrangements, whether written or oral funded or unfunded, in each case, that is sponsored, maintained, contributed to or required to be contributed to by the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, or any ERISA Affiliate, for the benefit of any current or former director, employee or independent contractor of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, or beneficiaries of such individuals, or with respect to which the Company or any of its Subsidiaries has or reasonably may have any liability (including, by reason of having an ERISA Affiliate): (i) “employee benefit plan” (within the meaning of Section 3(3) of ERISA, whether or not subject to ERISA); (ii) profit sharing, stock bonus, deferred compensation, bonus, stock option, stock purchase, restricted stock, equity incentive, phantom equity, pension, retirement, compensation, consulting, severance, retention, change in control, tax gross-up, indemnification, welfare, incentive or other compensation plan, program, agreement or arrangement; and (iii) plan, agreement or arrangement providing for “fringe benefits” or perquisites, whether funded or unfunded to employees, officers, directors or agents, including but not limited to benefits relating to automobiles, clubs, vacation, child care, parenting, sabbatical, sick leave and other paid time off, tuition reimbursement, medical, dental, hospitalization, life insurance, disability insurance and other types of insurance.

 

2
 

 

(e)      “Breach” shall mean with respect to a representation, warranty, covenant, obligation or other provision of this Agreement or any instrument delivered pursuant to this Agreement any inaccuracy in or breach of, or any failure to perform or comply with, such representation, warranty, covenant, obligation or other provision.

 

(f)      “Bank” shall mean North Shore Trust and Savings, a federal savings bank with its main office located in Waukegan, Illinois.

 

(g)      “Burdensome Condition” shall mean a condition issued by any Regulatory Authority that imposes restrictions, conditions or requirements on the activities of Purchaser, the Company or the Bank which would materially reduce the benefits of the Contemplated Transactions to such a degree that Purchaser or the Company would not, acting in a commercially reasonable manner, have entered into this Agreement had such conditions or requirements been known as of the date hereof.

 

(h)     “Business Day” shall mean any day except Saturday, Sunday and any day on which the Bank is authorized or required by law or other government action to close.

 

(i)      “Bylaws” shall mean the Bylaws of the Company, as amended.

 

(j)      “Call Reports” shall mean the quarterly reports of income and condition filed by the Bank with Regulatory Authorities.

 

(k)      “Charter” shall mean the Certificate of Incorporation of the Company, as amended.

 

(l)      “Code” shall mean the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

 

(m)     “Company Common Stock” shall mean the shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share.

 

(n)      “Company Preferred Stock” shall mean the shares of the Company’s preferred stock, par value $0.01 per share.

 

(o)     “Company Restricted Stock” shall mean shares of restricted Company Common Stock (whether granted by the Company pursuant to the Company Stock Plan, assumed by the Company in connection with any merger, acquisition or similar transaction or otherwise issued or granted).

 

(p)     “Company SEC Reports” shall mean the annual, quarterly and other reports, schedules, forms, statements and other documents (including exhibits and all other information incorporated therein) filed or furnished by the Company with the SEC under the Securities Act, the Exchange Act, or the regulations thereunder.

 

(q)    “Company Stockholder Approval” shall mean the adoption and approval of this Agreement and the Contemplated Transactions by the Company Stockholders, in accordance with Section 251 of the DGCL and the Charter, by the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Company Common Stock entitled to vote thereon, at the Company Stockholders’ Meeting.

 

3
 

 

(r)      “Company Stockholders” shall mean the holders of Company Common Stock.

 

(s)      “Company Stock Option” shall mean all options to purchase shares of Company Common Stock (whether granted by the Company pursuant to the Company Stock Plan, assumed by the Company in connection with any merger, acquisition or similar transaction or otherwise issued or granted).

 

(t)      “Company Stock Plan” shall mean the NSTS Bancorp, Inc. 2023 Equity Incentive Plan, and any successor plan to such plan.

 

(u)    “Company Transaction Expenses” shall mean shall mean any expenses, fees or costs incurred or accrued (or required to be accrued in accordance with GAAP) by the Company or any of its Subsidiaries in connection with this Agreement and the Contemplated Transactions, including, without limitation: (i) the aggregate fees and expenses of attorneys, accountants, consultants, financial advisors and other professional advisors incurred by the Company or any of its Subsidiaries in connection with this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions; (ii) any amounts paid or payable, as a result of the Contemplated Transactions, to any current or former director, officer or employee of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries under any contract, severance arrangement, stay bonus or retention arrangement, benefit plan or employment practice of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and all other payroll and related costs and expenses incurred by the Company or any of its Subsidiaries (including the employer portion of any payroll taxes in connection with the accelerated vesting and payouts related to the Company Stock Options and Company Restricted Stock); (iii) costs associated with the termination of any Benefit Plan in connection with the Contemplated Transactions; (iv) any costs associated with the termination of the Company’s and any of its Subsidiaries’ agreements with any of their vendors; (v) fees and costs associated with the preparation, printing and mailing of the Proxy Statement; (vi) any Remediation Cost; (vii) costs associated with Title Commitments and Title Insurance Policies pursuant to Section 6.10; and (viii) costs associated with the Mortgage Division Disposition; provided, however, that expenses of up to $105,000 incurred in connection with the Mortgage Division Disposition shall be excluded from the calculation of Company Transaction Expenses.

 

(v)      “Contemplated Transactions” shall mean all of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including: (i) the merger of the Merger Sub with and into the Company, with the Company as the surviving entity of such merger; (ii) the subsequent merger of the Company with and into Purchaser, with Purchaser as the surviving entity of such merger; (iii) the performance by each of Purchaser, the Company and Merger Sub of its respective covenants and obligations under this Agreement; (iv) Purchaser’s acquisition of control of the Bank; and (v) Purchaser’s payment of the Merger Consideration.

 

(w)     “Continuing Employees” shall mean each individual who is an employee of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries immediately prior to the Effective Time and continues to be an employee of Purchaser or one of its Subsidiaries immediately following the Effective Time.

 

4
 

 

(x)      “Contract” shall mean any agreement, contract, lease, obligation, promise or understanding (whether written or oral, and whether express or implied) that is legally binding, but excluding any such documents that the Company or any of its Subsidiaries has with its customers (e.g., loan or deposit agreements, lease financing agreements, business banking agreements, and cash management agreements): (i) under which a Person has or may acquire any rights; (ii) under which such Person has or may become subject to any obligation or liability; or (iii) by which such Person or any of the assets owned or used by such Person is or may become bound.

 

(y)      “DGCL” shall mean the Delaware General Corporation Law, as amended.

 

(z)      “ERISA” shall mean the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended.

 

(aa)    “ESOP” shall mean the North Shore Trust and Savings Employee Stock Ownership Plan.

 

(bb)    “ERISA Affiliate” shall mean, with respect to the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, any other Person that is, or at any relevant time was, part of the same “controlled group” for purposes of Section 4001(a)(14) of ERISA, deemed to be a “single employer” for purposes of Section 4001(b)(1) of ERISA, or deemed to be a “single employer” for purposes of Section 414(b), (c), (m), or (o) of the Code.

 

(cc)    “Exchange Act” shall mean the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.

 

(dd)    “Family” shall mean with respect to an individual: (i) the individual; (ii) the individual’s spouse and former spouses; and (iii) any other natural person who resides with such individual.

 

(ee)    “FDIC” shall mean the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

 

(ff)     “Federal Reserve” shall mean the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve system.

 

(gg)    “GAAP” shall mean generally accepted accounting principles in the United States.

 

(hh)    “ICFR” shall mean internal control over financial reporting.

 

(ii)     “Knowledge” shall mean: (i) with respect to the Company, those facts that are known or reasonably should have been known by the Chief Executive Officer, President, Chief Financial Officer, or Chief Lending Officer of the Company or its Subsidiaries; and (ii) with respect to Purchaser, those facts that are known or reasonably should have been known by the Chief Executive Officer, President or Chief Financial Officer of Purchaser.

 

5
 

 

(jj)     “Legal Requirement” shall mean any federal, state, local, municipal, or foreign Order, constitution, law, ordinance, regulation, rule, policy statement, directive, statute or treaty.

 

(kk)    “Material Adverse Effect” with respect to a Person shall mean an event, circumstance, change, effect or occurrence which, individually or together with any other event, circumstance, change, effect or occurrence: (i) is materially adverse to the business, financial condition, assets, liabilities or results of operations of such Person, taken as a whole; or (ii) materially impairs the ability of such Person to perform its obligations under this Agreement or to consummate the Contemplated Transactions on a timely basis; provided, however, that a Material Adverse Effect with respect to any Person that is a party hereto shall not include: (A) any change to the extent resulting from the announcement of this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions; (B) a change with respect to, or effect on, that Person and its Subsidiaries resulting from a change in law, rule, regulation, GAAP or regulatory accounting principles, as such would apply to the financial statements of such Person; (C) a change with respect to, or effect on, that Person or any of its Subsidiaries resulting from any other matter affecting depository institutions generally (including financial institutions and their holding companies), including changes in general political or economic conditions and changes in prevailing interest and deposit rates; (D) actions or omissions taken by that Person as required hereunder and actions or omissions by such Person with the prior written consent of the other parties hereto; (E) changes in national or international political or social conditions including the engagement by the United States in hostilities, whether or not pursuant to the declaration of a national emergency or war, or the occurrence of any military or terrorist attack upon or within the United States; and (F) any epidemics, pandemics, disease outbreaks, or other public health emergencies; except with respect to clauses (B), (C) (E) and (F), to the extent that the effects of such change are disproportionately adverse to the financial condition, results of operations or business of such Person taken as a whole, as compared to other companies in the industry in which such Person operates.

 

(ll)     “Material Interest” shall mean the direct or indirect beneficial ownership (as currently defined in Rule 13d-3 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended) of voting securities or other voting interests representing at least 25% of the outstanding voting power of a Person or equity securities or other equity interests representing at least 25% of the outstanding equity securities or equity interests in a Person.

 

(mm)  “OCC” shall mean the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

 

(nn)  “Order” shall mean any award, decision, injunction, judgment, order, ruling, supervisory letter, enforcement action, policy statement, memorandum of understanding, resolution, agreement, undertaking, directive, subpoena or verdict entered, issued, made, with, rendered or required by any court, administrative or other governmental agency, including any Regulatory Authority, or by any arbitrator.

 

6
 

 

(oo)    “Ordinary Course of Business” shall include any action taken by a Person only if such action:

 

(i)    is consistent in all material respects with the past practices of such Person, including with respect to quantity and nature, and is taken in the ordinary course of the normal day-to-day operations of such Person; and

 

(ii)    is in accordance in all material respects with all internal and regulatory policies, procedures and standards of such Person, including any lending policies.

 

(pp)    “Payout Spreadsheet” shall mean a spreadsheet attached hereto on the Agreement Date as Exhibit C, setting forth the following: (i) the Per Share Merger Consideration; (ii) the aggregate amount of the Option Payments; and (iii) the aggregate amounts of the Restricted Stock Payments, which shall be updated by the Company no later than five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date.

 

(qq)    “Per Share Merger Consideration” shall mean an amount equal to the quotient of (i) the Merger Consideration minus the aggregate amount of all Option Payments to be made to holders of Company Stock Options, divided by (ii) the number of shares of Company Common Stock issued and outstanding as of the Effective Time (which for the sake of clarity shall exclude the number of shares of Company Common Stock underlying the Company Stock Options), all as set forth on the Payout Spreadsheet.

 

(rr)    “Person” shall mean any individual, corporation (including any nonprofit corporation), general or limited partnership, limited liability company, joint venture, estate, trust, association, organization, labor union or other entity or any Regulatory Authority.

 

(ss)    “Pre-Closing Tax Period” shall mean any Taxable period ending on or before the Closing Date and, with respect to a Straddle Period, the portion of such Straddle Period ending on and including the Closing Date.

 

(tt)     “Proceeding” shall mean any action, arbitration, audit, hearing, litigation or suit (whether civil, criminal or administrative) commenced, brought, conducted or heard by or before, or otherwise involving, any judicial or governmental authority, including a Regulatory Authority, or arbitrator.

 

(uu)    “Regulation S-K” shall mean Regulation S-K promulgated under the Securities Act.

 

(vv)    “Regulatory Authority” shall mean any federal, state or local governmental body, court, agency or authority that, under applicable Legal Requirements: (i) has supervisory, judicial, administrative, police, taxing or other power or authority over Purchaser, the Company, or any of their respective Subsidiaries; (ii) is required to approve, or give its consent to, the Contemplated Transactions; or (iii) with which a filing must be made in connection therewith, including the FDIC, the Federal Reserve and the OCC.

 

(ww)   “Representative” shall mean with respect to a particular Person, any director, officer, manager, employee, agent, consultant, advisor or other representative of such Person, including legal counsel, accountants and financial advisors.

(xx)    “SEC” shall mean the United States Securities and Exchange Commission.

 

(yy)    “Securities Act” shall mean the Securities Act of 1933, as amended.

 

(zz)    “Straddle Period” shall mean any Taxable year or period beginning on or before and ending after the Closing Date.

 

(aaa)   “Subsidiary” shall mean, with respect to any Person means an affiliate controlled by such Person directly or indirectly through one or more intermediaries.

 

(bbb)   “Superior Proposal” shall mean a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal (with all references to “25%” in the definition of Acquisition Proposal being treated as references to “51%” for these purposes) which the board of directors of the Company concludes in good faith to be more favorable from a financial point of view to its stockholders than the Contemplated Transactions, (i) after receiving the advice of its financial advisor, (ii) after taking into account the likelihood and timing of consummation of the proposed transaction on the terms set forth therein (as compared to, and with due regard for, the terms herein) and (iii) after taking into account all legal (with the advice of outside counsel), financial (including the financing terms of any such proposal), regulatory (including the advice of outside counsel regarding the potential for regulatory approval of any such proposal) and other aspects of such proposal and any other relevant factors permitted under applicable Legal Requirements.

 

(ccc)   “Tax” shall mean any tax (including any income, gross receipts, capital gains, value-added, sales use, property, gift, estate, built-in gains, license, payroll, employment, excise, severance, stamp, occupation, premium, windfall profits, capital stock, franchise, withholding, social security, unemployment, disability, transfer, unclaimed property, escheat, non-income, estimated or any other tax), levy, assessment, tariff, duty (including any customs duty), deficiency or other fee, and any related charge or amount (including any fine, penalty, interest or addition to tax), imposed, assessed or collected by or under the authority of any Regulatory Authority or payable pursuant to any tax-sharing agreement or any other Contract relating to the sharing or payment of any such tax, levy, assessment, tariff, duty, deficiency or fee.

 

(ddd)   “Tax Return” shall mean any return (including any informational return), report, statement, schedule, notice, form or other document or information filed with or submitted to, or required to be filed with or submitted to, any Regulatory Authority in connection with the determination, assessment, collection or payment of any Tax or in connection with the administration, implementation or enforcement of or compliance with any Legal Requirement relating to any Tax.

 

(eee)   “Threatened” shall mean a claim, Proceeding, dispute, action or other matter for which any demand or statement has been made (orally or in writing) or any notice has been given (orally or in writing).

Section 1.2      Principles of Construction.

 

(a)      In this Agreement, unless otherwise stated or the context otherwise requires, the following uses apply: (i) actions permitted under this Agreement may be taken at any time and from time to time in the actor’s reasonable discretion; (ii) references to a statute shall refer to the statute and any successor statute, and to all regulations promulgated under or implementing the statute or successor, as in effect at the relevant time; (iii) in computing periods from a specified date to a later specified date, the words “from” and “commencing on” (and the like) mean “from and including,;” the words “to” and “until” (and the like) mean “to, but excluding;” and the words “ending on” (and the like) mean “to and including;” (iv) references to a governmental or quasi-governmental agency, authority or instrumentality shall also refer to a regulatory body that succeeds to the functions of the agency, authority or instrumentality; (v) indications of time of day mean Brookfield, Illinois time; (vi) “including” shall mean “including, but not limited to;” (vii) all references to sections, schedules and exhibits are to sections, schedules and exhibits in or to this Agreement unless otherwise specified; (viii) all words used in this Agreement will be construed to be of such gender or number as the circumstances require; (ix) the captions and headings of articles, sections, schedules and exhibits appearing in or attached to this Agreement have been inserted solely for convenience of reference and shall not be considered a part of this Agreement nor shall any of them affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement or any of its provisions; (x) any reference to a document or set of documents in this Agreement, and the rights and obligations of the parties under any such documents, shall mean such document or documents as amended from time to time, and any and all modifications, extensions, renewals, substitutions or replacements thereof; and (xi) “or” is not exclusive.

 

(b)      Unless otherwise specified herein, all references in this Agreement to schedules are to the disclosure schedules of the Company delivered to Purchaser before the Agreement Date and supplements thereto delivered pursuant to Section 6.4 (the “Schedules”). The Schedules consist of the agreements, lists, instruments and other documentation described or referred to in this Agreement with respect to the Bank or the Company, as applicable. Any item disclosed on any section to the Schedules shall be deemed to be fully disclosed with respect to all Schedules under which such item may be relevant and to the extent it is reasonably clear on the face of such Schedule that such item applies to such other Schedule. If there is any inconsistency between the statements in the body of this Agreement and those in the Schedules (other than an exception expressly set forth as such in the Schedules), the statements in the body of this Agreement will control.

 

(c)      All accounting terms not specifically defined herein shall be construed in accordance with the Accounting Standards.

 

(d)      With regard to each and every term and condition of this Agreement and any and all agreements and instruments subject to the terms hereof, the parties hereto understand and agree that the same have or has been mutually negotiated, prepared and drafted, and that if at any time the parties hereto desire or are required to interpret or construe any such term or condition or any agreement or instrument subject hereto, no consideration shall be given to the issue of which party hereto actually prepared, drafted or requested any term or condition of this Agreement or any agreement or instrument subject hereto.

ARTICLE 2

THE MERGER 

 

Section 2.1      The Merger. Provided that this Agreement shall not prior thereto have been terminated in accordance with its express terms, upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement and in accordance with the applicable provisions of the DGCL, at the Effective Time, Merger Sub shall be merged with and into the Company pursuant to the provisions of, and with the effects provided in, the DGCL, following which the separate corporate existence of Merger Sub shall cease and the Company will be the Surviving Entity.

 

Section 2.2      Closing; Effective Time.

 

(a)      The closing of the Contemplated Transactions (the “Closing”) shall occur on a date (the “Closing Date”) that is mutually agreed upon by the parties; provided, however, that in the absence of an agreement by either party, the Closing shall occur on the date that is five (5) Business Days after the satisfaction or waiver in writing of all of the conditions set forth in ARTICLE 8 and ARTICLE 9. The Closing shall occur via the exchange of documents electronically, through the mail or at a time and place that is mutually acceptable to Purchaser and the Company. Subject to the provisions of ARTICLE 10, failure to consummate the Contemplated Transactions on the date and time and at the place determined pursuant to this Section 2.2 will not by itself result in the termination of this Agreement and will not relieve any party of any obligation under this Agreement.

 

(b)      The parties hereto agree to file on or immediately prior to the Closing Date a certificate of merger with the Delaware Secretary of State (the “Delaware Certificate of Merger”). The Merger shall become effective as of the date specified in the Delaware Certificate of Merger (the “Effective Time”).

 

Section 2.3      Effects of the Merger. The Merger will have the effects specified in the DGCL. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Company will continue to be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and the separate corporate existence of the Company and all of its rights, privileges, powers and franchises, public as well as private, and all its debts, liabilities and duties as a corporation organized under the DGCL will continue unaffected by the Merger.

 

Section 2.4      Organizational Documents of the Surviving Entity. The certificate of incorporation and bylaws of Merger Sub, as in effect immediately prior to the Effective Time, shall be the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the Surviving Entity until thereafter amended in accordance with the provisions thereof and applicable Legal Requirements.

 

Section 2.5      Directors and Officers. The directors and officers of Merger Sub, as in office immediately prior to the Effective Time, shall be the directors and officers, respectively, of the Surviving Entity, from and after the Effective Time, until their successors have been duly elected or appointed and qualified or until their earlier death, resignation or removal in accordance with the terms of the Surviving Entity’s articles of incorporation, bylaws and the DGCL.

 

10
 

 

Section 2.6      Holding Company Merger. Prior to the Effective Time, the parties will cooperate and use their reasonable best efforts to effect the Holding Company Merger immediately following the Effective Time. At the effective time of the Holding Company Merger, the separate existence of the Company will terminate. Purchaser will be the surviving entity of the Holding Company Merger and will continue its existence under applicable Legal Requirements. The Holding Company Merger shall be accomplished pursuant to a merger agreement in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit D.

 

Section 2.7      Deliveries of Purchaser at Closing. At the Closing, Purchaser shall deliver the following items to the Company:

 

(a)      Evidence of the wire transfer to the Exchange Agent of an amount equal to the Conversion Fund and receipt by the Company of an amount equal to the Option Payments and Restricted Stock Payments pursuant to wire instructions delivered to Purchaser by the Company not less than three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date;

 

(b)      A certificate executed by Purchaser dated as of the Closing Date stating that: (i) all of the representations and warranties of Purchaser set forth in this Agreement are true and correct in all material respects with the same force and effect as if all of such representations and warranties were made at the Closing (except that to the extent such representations and warranties expressly relate to an earlier date, such representations shall be true and correct on and as of such earlier date); and (ii) Purchaser has performed or complied in all material respects with all of the covenants and obligations to be performed or complied with by it under the terms of this Agreement on or prior to the Closing; provided, however, that to the extent any representations and warranties, or performance and compliance with any covenants and obligations, are subject in this Agreement to a standard of Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard, such representations and warranties shall be true and correct in all respects, and Purchaser shall have performed and complied in all respects with such covenants and obligations, in each case to the extent of the Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard set forth herein;

 

(c)      Evidence of the Regulatory Approvals;

 

(d)      Copies of resolutions of the board of directors of Purchaser authorizing and approving this Agreement and the consummation of the Contemplated Transactions, certified as of the Closing Date by Purchaser; and

 

(e)      Such other documents as the Company or its counsel shall reasonably request.

 

All of such items shall be reasonably satisfactory in form and substance to the Company and its counsel.

 

Section 2.8      Deliveries of the Company at Closing. At the Closing, the Company shall deliver the following items to Purchaser:

 

(a)      Copies of resolutions of: (i) the board of directors of the Company; and (ii) the Company Stockholders; authorizing and approving this Agreement and the consummation of the Contemplated Transactions, certified as of the Closing Date by the Chief Executive Officer of the Company;

 

11
 

 

(b)      A resignation effective as of the Closing from each of the directors and officers of the Bank, as requested by Purchaser;

 

(c)      A certificate executed by the Chief Executive Officer of the Company dated as of the Closing Date stating that: (i) all of the representations and warranties of the Company set forth in this Agreement are true and correct in all material respects with the same force and effect as if all of such representations and warranties were made at the Closing (except that to the extent such representations and warranties expressly relate to an earlier date, such representations shall be true and correct on and as of such earlier date); and (ii) the Company has performed or complied in all material respects with all of the covenants and obligations to be performed or complied with by it under the terms of this Agreement on or prior to the Closing; provided, however, that to the extent any representations and warranties, or performance and compliance with any covenants and obligations, are subject in this Agreement to a standard of Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard, such representations and warranties shall be true and correct in all respects, and the Company shall have performed and complied in all respects with such covenants and obligations, in each case to the extent of the Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard set forth herein;

 

(d)      A good standing certificate for the Company issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware and dated as of the Closing Date;

 

(e)      A good standing certificate for the Bank issued by the OCC and dated not more than ten (10) Business Days prior to the Closing Date;

 

(f)      A copy of the Articles of Association of the Bank certified by the OCC and dated not more than ten (10) Business Days prior to the Closing Date;

 

(g)      A certificate of the Chief Executive Officer of the Bank dated as of the Closing Date: (i) certifying a copy of the Bylaws of the Bank; (ii) stating that there have been no further amendments to the Articles of Association of the Bank delivered pursuant to this Section 2.8; (iii) stating that the Company is the sole stockholder of the Bank; and (iv) stating that all Company Transaction Expenses have been paid or accrued by the Company or the Bank as of the Closing Date;

 

(h)      A certificate pursuant to Treasury Regulations Sections 1.1445-2(c)(3) and 1.897-2(h) duly executed by the Company, together with a form of notice to the IRS in accordance with the requirements of Treasury Regulations Section 1.897-2(h), in each case, in form and substance reasonably acceptable to Purchaser;

 

(i)       A copy of all executed ESOP Loan Termination Documentation; and

 

(j)       Such other documents as Purchaser or its counsel shall reasonably request.

 

All of such items shall be reasonably satisfactory in form and substance to Purchaser and its counsel.

Section 2.9      Withholding. Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, Purchaser will be entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts otherwise payable pursuant to this Agreement such amounts, if any, as Purchaser is required to deduct and withhold under the Code or any other applicable Legal Requirements; provided, however, that Purchaser shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide such party with written notice of its intent to withhold and permit the recipient to provide any documentation that might reduce or eliminate the withholding obligation, to the extent permitted by applicable Legal Requirements. Any amounts so deducted and withheld and paid over to or deposited with the appropriate taxing authority will be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the Person in respect of whom such deduction and withholding was made.

 

Section 2.10    Absence of Control. Subject to any specific provisions of this Agreement, it is the intent of the parties to this Agreement that Purchaser, by reason of this Agreement, shall not be deemed (until consummation of the Contemplated Transactions) to control, directly or indirectly, the Bank and shall not exercise, or be deemed to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling influence over the management or policies of the Bank.

 

ARTICLE 3

CONVERSION OF SECURITIES IN THE MERGER 

 

Section 3.1      Consideration.

 

(a)      The aggregate consideration to be paid in the Merger (the “Merger Consideration”) shall be an amount equal to $73,662,000 in cash, which amount shall be sufficient to pay (i) the Per Share Merger Consideration for each share of Company Common Stock issued and outstanding at Closing (inclusive of the aggregate amount of Restricted Stock Payments to be made to holders of Company Restricted Stock), and (ii) the aggregate amount of all Option Payments to be made to holders of Company Stock Options. In the event that the pre-tax amount of Company Transaction Expenses is greater than $4,500,000, then the Merger Consideration shall be reduced by an amount that is equal to such difference. There shall be no adjustment to the Merger Consideration in the event that the pre-tax amount of Company Transaction Expenses is less than or equal to $4,500,000.

 

(b)      Section 3.1(b) of the Schedules sets forth an itemized list and estimated dollar amount of the Company Transaction Expenses that can reasonably be determined as of the Agreement Date. Within five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, the Company shall deliver to Purchaser a final itemized list and dollar amount of the Company Transaction Expenses. All Company Transaction Expenses shall be accrued or paid by the Bank or the Company prior to the Effective Time.

 

Section 3.2      Cancellation of Shares.

 

(a)      At the Effective Time, each share of Company Common Stock (other than Dissenters’ Shares and shares held by Purchaser) issued and outstanding will no longer be outstanding and will automatically be cancelled and converted into the right to receive the Per Share Merger Consideration. Certificates (it being understood that any reference herein to a “certificate” be deemed to include reference to any book-entry account statement relating to the ownership of Company Common Stock) that represented Company Common Stock before the Effective Time will be deemed for all purposes to represent only the right to receive the Per Share Merger Consideration.

 

13
 

 

(b)      Notwithstanding anything in this Section 3.2 to the contrary, at the Effective Time and by virtue of the Merger, each share of Company Common Stock held in the Company’s treasury will be cancelled and no consideration will be issued or paid in exchange therefor.

 

(c)      Each share of common stock of Merger Sub issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time shall be converted into and become one (1) share of common stock, no par value per share, of the Surviving Entity.

 

Section 3.3      Exchange of Certificates. The exchange agent for purposes of this Agreement (the “Exchange Agent”) shall be selected by Purchaser and reasonably acceptable to the Company (which acceptance shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), and Purchaser shall execute and deliver any necessary exchange agent agreement at or prior to the Effective Time. Purchaser shall be solely responsible for the payment of any fees and expenses of the Exchange Agent.

 

(a)      At or prior to the Effective Time, Purchaser shall make available to the Exchange Agent, for the benefit of Company Stockholders for exchange in accordance with this ARTICLE 3 sufficient cash for payment of the Merger Consideration pursuant to Section 3.1 (less an amount equal to the aggregate amount of all Option Payments and Restricted Stock Payments, which amount will paid to the Company at least one (1) business day prior to the Effective Time for distribution through payroll of the Company or its applicable Subsidiary, or through such other process as agreed to by the parties, in each case in accordance with Section 3.4). Such amount of cash to be provided to the Exchange Agent as set forth in this Section 3.3(a) is referred to as the “Conversion Fund.”

 

(b)      As promptly as reasonably practicable after the Effective Time, but in no event later than five (5) Business Days after the Closing Date, Purchaser shall cause the Exchange Agent to mail to each holder of record of one or more certificates representing shares of Company Common Stock (“Company Stock Certificates”) a letter of transmittal (“Letter of Transmittal”), in a form to be agreed by the parties, which specifies, among other things, that delivery shall be effected, and risk of loss and title to Company Stock Certificates shall pass, only upon delivery of such certificates to the Exchange Agent, together with instructions for use in effecting the surrender of Company Stock Certificates pursuant to this Agreement.

 

(c)      Upon proper surrender of a Company Stock Certificate for exchange to the Exchange Agent, together with a properly completed and duly executed Letter of Transmittal, the holder of such Company Stock Certificate shall be entitled to receive in exchange therefor his, her or its Per Share Merger Consideration deliverable in respect of the shares of Company Common Stock represented by such Company Stock Certificate; thereupon such Company Stock Certificate shall forthwith be cancelled. No interest will be paid or accrued on the Per Share Merger Consideration deliverable upon surrender of a Company Stock Certificate.

 

14
 

 

(d)      After the Effective Time, there shall be no transfers on the stock transfer books of the Company of Company Common Stock.

 

(e)      Any portion of the Conversion Fund that remains unclaimed by the stockholders of the Company twelve (12) months after the Effective Time shall be paid to the Surviving Entity, or its successors in interest. Any Company Stockholders who have not theretofore complied with this ARTICLE 3 shall thereafter look only to the Surviving Entity, or its successors in interest, for payment of the Per Share Merger Consideration. Notwithstanding the foregoing, none of the Surviving Entity, the Exchange Agent or any other person shall be liable to any former holder of shares of Company Common Stock for any amount delivered in good faith to a public official pursuant to applicable abandoned property, escheat or similar laws.

 

(f)      In the event any Company Stock Certificate shall have been lost, stolen or destroyed, upon the making of an affidavit of that fact by the person claiming such Company Stock Certificate to be lost, stolen or destroyed and, if required by the Exchange Agent, the posting by such person of a bond in such amount as the Exchange Agent may determine is reasonably necessary as indemnity against any claim that may be made against it with respect to such Company Stock Certificate, the Exchange Agent will issue in exchange for such lost, stolen or destroyed Company Stock Certificate, and in accordance with this ARTICLE 3, the Per Share Merger Consideration.

 

Section 3.4      Treatment of Equity Awards.

 

(a)      Immediately prior to the Effective Time, by virtue of the Merger and without any further action on the part of the holders thereof, Purchaser, Merger Sub or the Company, each Company Stock Option that is outstanding as of immediately prior or the Effective Time, all of which such options shall be deemed vested as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, shall be canceled and automatically converted into the right to receive an amount in cash equal to the product of: (i) the total number of shares of Company Common Stock underlying such Company Stock Option, multiplied by (ii) the excess, if any, of (A) the Per Share Merger Consideration, over (B) the per share exercise price for such Company Stock Option (each, an “Option Payment”), net of any withholding Taxes required to be deducted and withheld by applicable Legal Requirements. Each Company Stock Option with a per share exercise price that is equal to or greater than the Per Share Merger Consideration shall be canceled at the Effective Time without the payment of consideration therefor. At least five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, the Company shall deliver to Purchaser a final list setting forth the name of each holder of Company Stock Options who will receive an Option Payment, and the amount of such Option Payment. Each Option Payment shall be payable on or as soon as administratively practicable following the Effective Time by the Company (or its applicable Subsidiary) through payroll, net of any withholding Taxes required to be deducted and withheld by applicable Legal Requirements; provided, that prior to the Effective Time, the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause each holder of the underlying Company Stock Option to deliver to the Company a cancellation agreement (a “Cancellation Agreement”), in a form reasonably satisfactory to Purchaser, acknowledging such holder’s right to the applicable Option Payment and releasing any claims such holder may have with respect to cancellation and conversion of each such Company Stock Option. No interest shall accrue or be paid on the amounts payable pursuant to this Section 3.4(a). To the extent that amounts are so deducted or withheld pursuant to this Section 3.4(a) and remitted to the appropriate governmental entity or other required recipient, such deducted or withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the person in respect of such deduction and withholding was made. The Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain an executed Cancellation Agreement from each holder of Company Stock Options prior to the Effective Time. In the event such a holder has not delivered a Cancellation Agreement prior to the Effective Time, the applicable Option Payment, net of any withholding Taxes required to be deducted and withheld by applicable Legal Requirements, shall be payable as soon as administratively practicable following delivery of the Cancellation Agreement by the holder, provided that such payment shall be made no later than the last day of the calendar year during which the Effective Time occurs.

 

15
 

 

(b)      Immediately prior to the Effective Time, by virtue of the Merger and without any further action on the part of the holders thereof, Purchaser, Merger Sub or the Company, each share of Company Restricted Stock that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time shall vest in full and the restrictions thereon shall lapse, and, as of the Effective Time, each such share of Company Restricted Stock shall be considered outstanding shares of Company Common Stock and automatically converted into the right to receive the Per Share Merger Consideration (each, a “Restricted Stock Payment”); provided that each Restricted Stock Payment shall be payable on or as soon as administratively practicable following the Effective Time by the Company (or its applicable Subsidiary) through payroll, net of any withholding Taxes required to be deducted and withheld by applicable Legal Requirements. To the extent that amounts are so deducted or withheld pursuant to this Section 3.4(b) and remitted to the appropriate governmental entity or other required recipient, such deducted or withheld amounts shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as having been paid to the person in respect of such deduction and withholding was made. No interest shall accrue or be paid on the amounts payable pursuant to this Section 3.4(b). At least five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, the Company shall deliver to Purchaser a final list setting forth the name of each holder of Company Restricted Stock who will receive a Restricted Stock Payment, and the amount of such Restricted Stock Payment.

 

(c)      Prior to the Closing, the Company, or the appropriate committee of the board of directors of the Company, as applicable, shall take any and all such actions as are necessary, including the adoption of appropriate resolutions, to give effect to the transactions contemplated by this Section 3.4, including to provide that the Company Stock Plan and all awards issued thereunder will terminate as of the Effective Time, subject to payment as provided in this Section 3.4.

REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE COMPANY 

 

The Company hereby represents and warrants to Purchaser as follows:

Section 4.4      No Conflict. Neither the execution or delivery of this Agreement nor the consummation or performance of any of the Contemplated Transactions will, directly or indirectly (with or without notice or lapse of time): (a) contravene, conflict with or result in a violation of any provision of the Charter, the Bylaws or the charter or bylaws of the Bank, each as in effect on the Agreement Date, or any currently effective resolution adopted by the board of directors or stockholder(s) of either the Bank or the Company; (b) contravene, conflict with or result in a violation of, or give any Regulatory Authority or other Person the valid and enforceable right to challenge any of the Contemplated Transactions or to exercise any remedy or obtain any relief under, any Legal Requirement or any Order to which the Bank or the Company, or any of their respective assets that are owned or used by them, may be subject, except for any contravention, conflict or violation that is permissible by virtue of obtaining the Regulatory Approvals necessitated by the Contemplated Transactions, including such approvals under the Change in Bank Control Act, as amended; (c) contravene, conflict with or result in a violation or breach of any provision of, or give any Person the right to declare a default or exercise any remedy under, or to accelerate the maturity or performance of, or to cancel, terminate or modify any Contract to which the Bank is a party or by which any of its assets is bound; or (d) result in the creation of any lien, charge or encumbrance upon or with respect to any of the assets owned or used by the Bank; except, in the case of each of clauses (c) and (d), where any such contravention, conflict, violation, breach, lien, charge or encumbrance would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect on the Bank. Except: (i) as set forth on Section 4.4 of the Schedules; (ii) for the approval or confirmation of non-review by the SEC of the Proxy Statement (as defined in Section 6.6); (iii) for the Company Stockholders Approval referred to in Section 6.6; and (iv) the approvals referred to Section 8.1, neither the Bank nor the Company is or will be required to give any notice to or obtain any consent from any Person in connection with the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the consummation or performance of any of the Contemplated Transactions.

Section 4.5      Company Capitalization.

(b)      The Bank’s loan files contain all notes, leases and other necessary evidences of any Bank Loan, including all loan agreements, loan participation agreements and certificates, security agreements, mortgages, guarantees, amendments, uniform commercial code financing statements and similar documents evidencing collateral or other financial accommodations relating to the Bank Loans (“Loan Documents”). All Loan Documents are correct in amount and were given for valid consideration. None of the obligations represented by the Loan Documents has been modified, altered, forgiven, discharged or otherwise disposed of except as indicated by the Loan Documents or as a result of bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium or similar laws relating to or affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally or equitable principles or doctrines.

(a) To the Knowledge of the Company, there has not been any security breach or other compromise that has caused or would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect on the Company or its Subsidiaries (“Security Breach”) relating to the Company’s or its Subsidiaries’ information technology and computer systems, networks, hardware, software, data and databases (including the data and information of their respective customers, employees, suppliers, vendors and any third party data maintained by or on behalf of them), equipment or technology (collectively, “IT Systems and Data”); (b) neither the Company nor its Subsidiaries have been notified of, and have no Knowledge of any event or condition that would reasonably be expected to result in, any Security Breach to their IT Systems and Data; and (c) the Company and its Subsidiaries have implemented appropriate controls, policies, procedures and technological safeguards to maintain and protect the integrity, continuous operation, redundancy and security of their IT Systems and Data reasonably consistent with industry standards and practices, or as required by applicable regulatory standards. ARTICLE 5

REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF PURCHASER 

 

Purchaser hereby represents and warrants to the Company as follows:

 

Section 5.1      Corporate Organization. Purchaser is a corporation duly organized, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Except for First National Bank of Brookfield, a national bank with its main office located in Brookfield, Illinois, Purchaser has no Subsidiaries. Purchaser is registered with the Federal Reserve as a bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. Purchaser has full power and authority, corporate and otherwise, to own, operate and lease its properties as presently owned, operated and leased, and to carry on its business as it is now being conducted.

 

40
 

 

Section 5.2      Authorization; Enforceability. Purchaser has the requisite corporate power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Agreement. The execution and delivery of this Agreement and the consummation of the Contemplated Transactions have been duly and validly authorized by Purchaser’s board of directors. Purchaser’s board of directors has determined that the Contemplated Transactions, on substantially the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, are in the best interests of Purchaser and its stockholders. The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Purchaser, and the consummation by Purchaser of its obligations under this Agreement, have been authorized by all necessary corporate action and, subject to the receipt of the Regulatory Approvals, this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid and binding obligation of Purchaser enforceable in accordance with its terms, except as such enforcement may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization or other Legal Requirements affecting creditors’ rights generally and subject to general principles of equity.

 

Section 5.3      No Conflict. Neither the execution nor delivery of this Agreement nor the consummation or performance of any of the Contemplated Transactions will, directly or indirectly (with or without notice or lapse of time): (a) contravene, conflict with or result in a violation of any provision of the Certificate of Incorporation or Bylaws of Purchaser each as in effect on the date hereof; or (b) assuming receipt of the Regulatory Approvals, contravene, conflict with or result in a violation of any Legal Requirement or any Order to which Purchaser may be subject, except for any contravention, conflict or violation that is permissible by virtue of obtaining the Regulatory Approvals.

 

Section 5.4      Sufficient Funds. Purchaser hereby confirms that it has, or will have, sufficient cash on hand to fund the payment of the Merger Consideration at the time of the Closing.

 

Section 5.5      Approval Delays. No facts or circumstances exist related to the condition of or operation of Purchaser or its Subsidiaries that, to Purchaser’s Knowledge, may prevent or unreasonably delay Purchaser’s receipt of the Regulatory Approvals. The most recent CRA rating of First National Bank of Brookfield was “satisfactory.”

 

ARTICLE 6

COVENANTS OF THE COMPANY 

 

Section 6.1      Access and Investigation. Following the Agreement Date, for purposes of Purchaser’s continuing due diligence review of the Company and its Subsidiaries and for monitoring compliance by the Company with the terms of this Agreement, Purchaser and its Representatives shall at all times during normal business hours and with not less than three (3) Business Days advance notice, have reasonable access to the facilities, operations, records and properties of the Company and its Subsidiaries in accordance with the provisions of this Section 6.1 to the extent permitted under applicable law provided such access is consented to in writing or by electronic mail by the Company and reasonably designed not to interrupt the business of the Company or its Subsidiaries. Notwithstanding any other provision in this Agreement, Purchaser shall not contact the Bank’s customers, vendors or other contractual counterparties or employees or officers without the express written consent, and full coordination with, the Company or its Subsidiaries. Purchaser and its Representatives may make or cause to be made such reasonable investigation of the operations, records and properties of the Company and its Subsidiaries and of its financial and legal condition as Purchaser shall deem necessary or advisable to familiarize itself with such records, properties and other matters; provided, however, that such access or investigation shall not interfere unnecessarily with the normal operations of the Bank. The Company shall upon written request provide to Purchaser copies of all information provided to the board of directors of the Bank, or committees thereof, in connection with any meetings or otherwise and any other financial reports or other analyses prepared by or for senior management of the Bank since January 1, 2024. This Section 6.1 shall not require the disclosure of any information the disclosure of which to Purchaser would be prohibited by any Legal Requirement, including any confidential supervisory information, or any information arising out of or related to this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions that is subject to attorney-client privilege and Purchaser agrees that any information provided to it by the Company or any of its Subsidiaries in accordance with this Section 6.1 shall be used by it only in connection with this Agreement and for no other purpose and that all such information shall be treated confidentially.

Section 6.2      Operation of the Company and its Subsidiaries.

 

(a)      Between the Agreement Date and the Closing, the Company shall, and shall cause each of its Subsidiaries to:

 

(i)      conduct its business only in the Ordinary Course of Business and in compliance in all material respects with all Legal Requirements and all Contracts, except as may otherwise be required herein;

 

(ii)     use its commercially reasonable efforts to preserve intact its current business organization, keep available the services of its current officers, employees and agents, and maintain the goodwill of its suppliers, customers, landlords, creditors, employees, agents and others who have business relationships with it;

 

(iii)    provide the following information in a monthly report to Purchaser: (A) the Bank’s board package (except for any information subject to privilege or that would constitute confidential supervisory information, including any information related to this Agreement or the Contemplated Transaction); (B) monthly financial statements; and (C) a Bank Loan past due report;

 

(iv)    maintain all of its assets necessary for the conduct of its business in as good of operating condition and repair as they are now in, reasonable wear and tear and insured casualty damage excepted;

 

(v)     maintain policies of insurance upon its assets and with respect to the conduct of its business in amounts and kinds comparable to that in effect on the Agreement Date and pay all premiums on such policies when due;

 

(vi)    file in a timely manner all required filings with all Regulatory Authorities and cause such filings to be true and correct;

 

(vii)   promptly notify Purchaser of any Bank Loan risk rating upgrades or downgrades;

(viii)  promptly notify Purchaser of any proposed resignations or terminations of employment of employees; and

 

(ix)    maintain its books, accounts and records in the Ordinary Course of Business, on a basis consistent with prior years.

 

(b)      Consistent with the foregoing, between the Agreement Date and the Closing, except with the prior written consent of Purchaser, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed or denied, the Company shall not, and the Company shall cause the Bank not to:

 

(i)      change its authorized or issued capital stock or grant any stock option or right to purchase shares of its capital stock or issue any security convertible into such capital stock or evidence of indebtedness (except in/ connection with customer deposits) or grant any registration rights;

 

(ii)     issue, sell, or deliver, or agree or commit to issue, sell or deliver, any Company Common Stock or common stock of the Bank (whether through the issuance or granting of options, restricted stock, restricted stock units, warrants, commitments, subscriptions, rights to purchase, any equity or equity-based instruments, or otherwise), except: (A) the issuance, delivery or sale of shares of Company Common Stock pursuant to Company Restricted Stock awards or Company Stock Options or pursuant to the Company Stock Plan in accordance with its terms; or (B) as required by any Benefit Plan in effect on the Agreement Date;

 

(iii)    directly or indirectly acquire, repurchase or redeem any securities, except for: (A) with respect to Company Common Stock pursuant to the terms and conditions of Company Restricted Stock awards or Company Stock Options outstanding as of the Agreement Date in accordance with their terms or to otherwise satisfy Tax obligations with respect to awards granted pursuant to the Company Stock Plan or to pay the exercise price of Company Stock Options, in each case in accordance with the existing terms of the applicable Company Stock Plan as in effect on the Agreement Date; (B) transactions between the Company and any of its direct or indirect Subsidiaries; or (C) transactions otherwise required to be taken by the ESOP or in connection with the termination of an outstanding ESOP Loan;

 

(iv)    invest or take any actions to inject any additional capital or equity into the Bank other than pursuant to Legal Requirements or prudent banking principles and increases in the Bank’s capital accounts arising due to earnings in the Ordinary Course of Business;

 

(v)     declare or pay any dividend or other distribution or payment in respect of shares of its capital stock other than dividends paid to the Company for the purpose of distributing to stockholders of the Company dividends to pay for income taxes in the Ordinary Course of Business;

(xi)    make any Bank Loan that does not comply with Bank’s loan policy or other policies, procedures and standards of Bank (other than pursuant to standard exceptions thereto);

 

(xii)   many any new Bank Loan or commit to renew, extend the term of or increase the amount of any existing Bank Loan other than in the Ordinary Course of Business;

 

(xiii)  make any new Bank Loan, or commit to make a new Bank Loan, or renew, extend the term of or increase the amount of any existing Bank Loan if such Bank Loan is (A) an unsecured Bank Loan, or (B) a secured Bank Loan in an amount exceeding 400,000; provided, however, that Bank may make such a Bank Loan in the event (x) the Bank has delivered to Purchaser or its designated Representative a notice of its intention to make such Bank Loan and such information, including any internally-prepared loan presentation, as Purchaser or its designated Representative shall reasonably require in respect thereof, and (y) Purchaser or its designated Representative shall not have objected to such Bank Loan by giving written notice of such objection within two (2) Business Days following delivery to Purchaser or its designated Representative the notice of intention and required information; provided, further, that this section shall not apply to Bank Loans that are single family mortgage loans that are qualified to be sold and will be sold within thirty (30) days of origination;

(xvii) transfer to the Company or any of its Affiliates any of the assets or deposits of the Bank;

(xx)   merge or consolidate with or into any other Person, or acquire any stock, equity interest or business of any other Person other than in the Ordinary Course of Business with respect to foreclosures on pledged collateral;

 

(xxi)  file an application to open a new office or branch, close a current office or branch or relocate the operations of a branch from an existing location;

 

(xxii) purchase, acquire, sell, transfer, dispose or reinvest any investment securities;

 

(xxiii) purchase or acquire any investments, direct or indirect, in any derivative securities, financial futures or commodities or enter into any interest rate swap, floors and option agreements, or other similar interest rate management agreements;

Section 6.3      Subsequent Bank Financial Statements. As soon as reasonably available after the Agreement Date, and in the case of monthly financial statements, not later than ten (10) days after month-end, the Company will furnish Purchaser copies of: (a) internally prepared monthly financial statements of the Bank that are provided to the directors of the Bank; and (b) all other financial reports or statements submitted after the Agreement Date by the Bank to any Regulatory Authority, to the extent not available online and as permitted by law (the “Internal Financial Reports”). Additionally, except as may be required by changes in the Accounting Standards or Legal Requirements effective after the Agreement Date, all Call Reports of the Bank for each quarterly or annual period completed after the Agreement Date (the “Subsequent Bank Financial Statements”), shall be prepared on a basis consistent with past accounting practices and shall fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Bank for the dates and periods presented. The Subsequent Bank Financial Statements, and to the Knowledge of the Company, the Internal Financial Reports, will not include any material assets or omit to state any material liabilities or other facts, which inclusion or omission would render such Subsequent Bank Financial Statements misleading in any material respect.

 

Section 6.4      Advice of Changes. Between the Agreement Date and the Closing, the Company shall promptly notify Purchaser in writing if it becomes aware of any fact or condition that causes or constitutes a Breach of any of its representations and warranties as of the Agreement Date, or if the Company becomes aware of the occurrence after the Agreement Date of any fact or condition that would (except as expressly contemplated by this Agreement) cause or constitute a Breach of any such representation or warranty had such representation or warranty been made as of the time of occurrence or discovery of such fact or condition. If any such fact or condition would require any change in the Schedules if such Schedules were dated the date of the occurrence or discovery of any such fact or condition, the Company will promptly deliver to Purchaser a supplement to the Schedules specifying such change; provided, however, that any such supplement will not cure any Breach by the Company of this Agreement. During the same period, the Company will promptly notify Purchaser of the occurrence of any Breach of any of its covenants in this Agreement or of the occurrence of any event that might reasonably be expected to make the satisfaction of the conditions in ARTICLE 8 impossible or unlikely.

Section 6.5      Other Offers. The Company agrees that it will not, and will not authorize or permit any of its Representatives to, initiate, solicit, encourage or knowingly facilitate inquiries or proposals with respect to, or engage in any negotiations concerning, or provide any confidential or nonpublic information or data to, or have any discussions with, any Person relating to, any Acquisition Proposal; provided, that, in the event the Company receives an unsolicited bona fide Acquisition Proposal from a Person other than Purchaser after the Agreement Date, and the board of directors of the Company concludes in good faith that such Acquisition Proposal constitutes a Superior Proposal or would reasonably be likely to result in a Superior Proposal and, after considering the advice of outside counsel, that failure to take such actions would be reasonably likely to result in a violation of the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable Legal Requirements, the Company may: (a) furnish information with respect to the Company and the Bank to such Person making such Acquisition Proposal pursuant to a customary confidentiality agreement (subject to the requirement that any such information not previously provided to Purchaser shall be promptly furnished to Purchaser); (b) participate in discussions or negotiations regarding such Acquisition Proposal; and (c) terminate this Agreement in order to concurrently enter into an agreement with respect to such Acquisition Proposal; provided, however, that the Company may not terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 6.5 unless and until (i) five (5) Business Days have elapsed following the delivery to Purchaser of a written notice of such determination by the board of directors of the Company, and, during such five (5) Business Day period, to the extent that Purchaser so requests, the Company and Purchaser cooperate with one another with the intent of enabling the parties to engage in good faith negotiations so that the Contemplated Transactions may be completed, and (ii) at the end of such five (5) Business Day period, the Company continues, in good faith and after consultation with outside legal counsel and financial advisor, to believe that a Superior Proposal continues to exist.

 

Section 6.6      Proxy Statement; Company Stockholder Approval.

 

(a)      As soon as reasonably practicable following the Agreement Date, but no later than forty-five (45) days after the Agreement Date, the Company shall prepare and file with the SEC a preliminary proxy statement prepared by the Company for use in connection with the Company Stockholders’ Meeting (as defined below), prepared in accordance with the DGCL, the rules and regulations of the SEC, and other Legal Requirements (the “Proxy Statement”). Prior to the filing of the Proxy Statement, the Company shall consult with Purchaser with respect to such filing and shall afford Purchaser and its representatives reasonable opportunity to review and comment thereon. The Proxy Statement shall include all information reasonably requested by Purchaser to be included. The Company will advise Purchaser, promptly after it receives notice thereof, of the time when any supplement or amendment has been filed, any request by the SEC to amend the Proxy Statement or comments thereon and responses thereto or requests by the SEC for additional information. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond (with the assistance of the other party) as promptly as practicable to any comments of the SEC with respect thereto. The Company will use its commercially reasonable efforts to file a definitive version of the Proxy Statement and cause the Proxy Statement to be mailed to the Company Stockholders as promptly as practicable after the earlier of (i) 10 days after the filing of the preliminary Proxy Statement, if the SEC has confirmed that it will not review the Proxy Statement and (ii) the SEC’s review and approval of the Proxy Statement. If prior to the Effective Time any event occurs with respect to the Company, Purchaser or any Subsidiary of the Company or Purchaser, respectively, or any change occurs with respect to information supplied by or on behalf of the Company or Purchaser, respectively, for inclusion in the Proxy Statement that is required to be described in an amendment of, or a supplement to, the Proxy Statement, the Company or Purchaser, as applicable, shall promptly notify the other of such event (including, prior to entering into any agreement providing for any merger, consolidation, amalgamation, share exchange, business combination, issuance of securities, acquisition of securities, tender offer, exchange offer or other similar transaction involving Purchaser or any of its Subsidiaries), and the Company or Purchaser, as applicable, shall cooperate in the prompt filing with the SEC of any necessary amendment or supplement to the Proxy Statement and, as required by applicable Legal Requirements, in disseminating the information contained in such amendment or supplement to the Company Stockholders and, except as otherwise set forth in this Agreement, no amendment or supplement (including by incorporation by reference) to the Proxy Statement shall be made without the approval of Purchaser, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

(b)      The Company’s board of directors shall recommend to the Company Stockholders the approval of this Agreement, shall solicit from the Company Stockholders proxies voting only in favor thereof, and shall not withdraw, modify or change, in any manner adverse to Purchaser, or publicly announce its intent to withdraw, modify or change, in any manner adverse to Purchaser, such recommendation of this Agreement; provided, however, that the Company shall not be required to make the recommendation required by this Section 6.6, and shall be permitted to withdraw, modify or change such recommendation, if the Company’s board of directors determines, in good faith, that the exercise of its fiduciary duties to the Company Stockholders under applicable Legal Requirements, as advised by its counsel, so requires.
