(a)      All transfer, documentary, sales, use, stamp, registration, value added, or other Taxes and fees (including penalties and interest) incurred in connection with the Contemplated Transactions shall be borne and paid by the Company when due. The Company shall, at its own expense, timely file any Tax Return or other document with respect to such Taxes or fees (and Purchaser shall cooperate with respect thereto as reasonably necessary).

 

(b)      Purchaser, the Company and each of its Subsidiaries shall provide each other with such cooperation and information as may be reasonably necessary in the filing of any Tax Return or in connection with any Proceeding in respect of Taxes of the Company and each of its Subsidiaries.

 

48
 

 

(c)      With respect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, without the prior written consent of Purchaser, the Company shall not (i) make, change or rescind any election inconsistent with prior Tax Returns, (ii) amend any Tax Return or take any position on any Tax Return inconsistent with prior filings, or (iii) settle or compromise any liability with respect to Taxes.

 

(d)      The parties hereto acknowledge that the Company’s Subsidiaries will become members of a consolidated group together with Purchaser effective as of the Closing Date and that the taxable year of each of the Company’s Subsidiaries will end as of the end of Closing Date pursuant to Treasury Regulation Section 1.1502-76(b)(1)(ii)(A)(1). The parties further acknowledge that, as a result of the Holding Company Merger, the Company will cease to exist as a separate legal entity as of the Closing Date.

 

(e)      All tax sharing agreements or arrangements binding on the Company or any of its Subsidiaries shall terminate as of the Closing Date, and neither the Company nor any of its Subsidiaries shall have any further liability or obligation thereunder from and after the Closing Date.

 

Section 6.9      Consents; Third Party Approvals. As soon as practicable after the Agreement Date, the Bank shall use its commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the approvals set forth on Section 4.4 of the Schedules.

 

Section 6.10    Title to Real Estate.

 

(a)      As soon as practical after the Agreement Date, but in any event no later than forty-five (45) days after the Agreement Date, the Company shall obtain and deliver to Purchaser, with respect to all interests in real property owned by the Bank, other than property carried as OREO, a commitment for an owner’s title insurance policy (collectively, the “Title Commitments”), issued by a title company selected by the Company and reasonably acceptable to Purchaser (the “Title Company”), showing fee simple title or a valid leasehold interest, as applicable, in the Bank in such real property with coverage over all standard exceptions (provided Purchaser obtains the Surveys (as defined in Section 6.11 below)) and subject to no liens, mortgages, security interests, encumbrances or charges of any kind except for any Permitted Encumbrances. The cost of obtaining any preliminary report of title discussed in this Section 6.10(a) shall be borne by the Company. With respect to property carried as OREO, the Company shall provide reasonably acceptable written proof of ownership by the Bank of such OREO property.

 

(b)      At the Closing, the Company shall obtain at its own expense and deliver to Purchaser, with respect to all interests in real property owned by the Bank, an owner’s title insurance policy or leasehold title insurance policy, as applicable (collectively, the “Title Insurance Policies”), or an irrevocable commitment to issue such a policy to Purchaser at no expense to Purchaser (other than the cost of any endorsements to the Title Policies requested by Purchaser, which costs shall be borne by Purchaser) dated as of the later of the Closing Date and the actual date of recording of the deed for such property, on ALTA Policy Form 2006 or Form 2021, if available (if not available, then on Form B-1992), with respect to all interests in real property owned or leased, as applicable, by the Bank, other than property carried as OREO, issued by the Title Company, subject to only such exceptions as are Permitted Encumbrances or have been otherwise accepted by Purchaser, containing any endorsements reasonably required by Purchaser, insuring the fee simple estate of the Bank in the such properties in the amount not less than the greater of (i) the appraised value of the property and (ii) the value at which the Bank currently carries the property on its books, subject only to the Permitted Encumbrances.

 

49
 

 

(c)      Except for Permitted Encumbrances, neither the Company nor any of its Subsidiaries shall voluntarily encumber any real property prior to the Closing Date. In the event that the Company cannot obtain any of the Title Insurance Policies, and Purchaser has not, prior to the Closing Date, given notice to the Company that Purchaser is willing to waive objection to each title exception which is not set forth in the applicable Title Commitment, excluding such exceptions which constitute a Permitted Encumbrance (each, a “New Encumbrance”), the Company shall discharge or remove each such New Encumbrance that can be discharged or removed by the payment of a liquidated sum of money. The Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to discharge any New Encumbrance that cannot be discharged solely by the payment of a liquidated sum of money, unless such New Encumbrance is a Permitted Encumbrance. The Company shall be entitled to postpone the Closing Date for up to thirty (30) days in the aggregate, in order to discharge any New Encumbrance which is not a Permitted Encumbrance.

 

(d)      If the consent of any landlord is required for transfer or assignment of any lease by virtue of the Contemplated Transactions, the Company shall obtain such required consents as soon as reasonably practicable after the Agreement Date, but in no event later than three (3) Business Days before the Closing.

 

Section 6.11    Surveys. Purchaser may, in its discretion, within forty-five (45) days after the Agreement Date, require the Company to provide, at Purchaser’s expense and as soon as practicable, but in no event later than fifteen (15) Business Days prior to the Closing, a current American Land Title Association survey, including any Table A items reasonably requested by Purchaser (each a “Survey” and collectively, the “Surveys”), of any or all parcels of real property owned by the Bank, other than property carried as OREO, disclosing no survey defects that would materially impair the use thereof for the purposes for which it is held or materially impair the value of such property.

 

Section 6.12    Environmental Investigation.

 

(a)      Purchaser may, in its discretion and at Purchaser’s expense, within forty-five (45) days after the Agreement Date, complete a Phase I environmental site assessment in accordance with ASTM Standard E1527-21, Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments (the “ASTM Standard”) to be delivered to the Company and Purchaser for each Owned Real Estate parcel (each, a “Phase I Report”), conducted by an independent professional consultant selected by Purchaser and reasonably acceptable to the Company to determine if any Owned Real Estate contains or gives evidence of any “Recognized Environmental Conditions,” as that term is defined in the ASTM Standard.

 

50
 

 

(b)      If a Phase I Report discloses any “Recognized Environmental Conditions” under the ASTM Standard, then Purchaser may, promptly obtain a Phase II subsurface investigation with respect to any Recognized Environmental Condition identified in a Phase I, which report shall, to the extent feasible, contain an estimate of the approximate cost of any remediation or other follow-up work recommended to address those conditions in accordance with applicable Legal Requirements (each, a “Phase II Report,”  and, together with the associated Phase I Report, an “Environmental Report”). The subject, scope, manner and method of each Phase II Report will be subject to the Company’s prior review and written approval, which shall not be unreasonably delayed, conditioned, or withheld. The cost of each such Phase II Report shall be borne by Purchaser and shall be provided to both the Company and Purchaser. In addition, if requested by the Company, Purchaser does hereby agree to restore at its cost any Owned Real Estate for which it has undertaken an environmental investigation pursuant to this Section 6.12 to the condition existing immediately prior to such investigation. Purchaser shall have no duty to act upon any information produced by an Environmental Report. If any Phase II Report confirms the presence of environmental contamination which requires remediation under applicable Environmental Laws, the Company shall cause such remediation work to be performed, at its own cost (the “Remediation Cost”), by an environmental remediation firm mutually agreed to by Purchaser and Company. The Remediation Cost shall be accrued or paid by the Company prior to Closing.

 

Section 6.13    Landlord Estoppels. Not less than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing, the Company shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide estoppel certificates executed by the landlords under the Leases in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit E.

 

Section 6.14    Company Voting Agreement. Concurrently with the execution and delivery of this Agreement, the Company shall deliver to Purchaser the Company Voting Agreement, signed by all of the directors and executive officers of the Company as of the Agreement Date who own or control the voting of any shares of Company Common Stock.

 

Section 6.15    Leases and Contracts. The Company agrees to cooperate and coordinate in good faith with Purchaser in the negotiation of any new or renewal or extension of (i) any existing Contract, involving an obligation by the Bank of more than $25,000, including the Bank’s data processing agreement, or (ii) any existing Leases involving an obligation by the Bank of more than $25,000 with the purpose of achieving the best possible economic and business result for Purchaser, the Company and its Subsidiaries in light of the Contemplated Transactions. The Company agrees to request from the counterparty information and clarification of the terms of any Contract if requested by Purchaser.

 

Section 6.16    Mortgage Division. On or prior to the Closing Date, the Company shall cause the Bank to complete the disposition of the Bank’s Oak Leaf Community Mortgage division (the “Mortgage Division”) in accordance with the provisions set forth in Section 6.16 of the Schedules (the “Mortgage Division Disposition”). Section 6.16 of the Schedules sets forth a true, correct, and complete list, as of the date hereof, of the following: (x) the name, title, and current employment status of each employee employed in or primarily dedicated to the Mortgage Division; (y) each written or oral contract, agreement, lease, license, or other binding commitment primarily related to the operation of the Mortgage Division; and (z) a description of all material assets owned, leased, licensed, or otherwise used by the Mortgage Division, including all material real and personal property and intellectual property rights.

 

51
 

 

Section 6.17    Certain Employee Benefit Matters.

 

(a)      The Company shall take (or cause the Bank to take) all actions necessary to terminate the severance policies covering any employees of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries, if any, immediately prior to the Effective Time. From and after the Effective Time, Purchaser (or Purchaser’s applicable Subsidiary) will cause any eligible Continuing Employee, other than a Continuing Employee eligible to receive severance benefits or other similar payments or benefits as a result of the Contemplated Transactions under any employment, change in control, severance, or any other agreement or arrangement, to be covered by a severance policy under which such employees who incur a qualifying involuntary termination of employment without cause will be eligible to receive severance pay in accordance with the severance pay schedule set forth on Section 6.17(a) of the Schedules.

 

(b)      The Company shall provide (or cause its applicable Subsidiary to provide) Purchaser true and complete copies of any and all Code Section 280G calculations (including any valuations reports for valuation of restrictive covenants in connection with such Code Section 280G calculations) prepared with respect to any disqualified individual in connection with the Contemplated Transactions.

 

Section 6.18    ESOP Matters.

 

(a)      Prior to the Effective Time, the Bank shall have taken or caused to be taken all such actions as may be necessary to terminate the ESOP, and adopt corresponding amendments to the ESOP documents (which amendments shall be in form and substance acceptable to Purchaser) effective as of the date not later than the Closing Date (the “ESOP Termination Date”), but conditioned upon the Closing occurring. Such amendments to the ESOP shall provide: (i) that the ESOP is no longer required to be invested in Company Common Stock; (ii) that no new participants or former participants shall be admitted to the ESOP on or after the ESOP Termination Date and no contributions will be made to the ESOP on or after the ESOP Termination Date; (iii) that all ESOP participant accounts shall be fully vested as of the ESOP Termination Date; (iv) that the entire balance of the account of a participant or beneficiary of the ESOP will be required to be distributable in cash in a lump-sum payment; (v) that the ESOP shall be terminated effective as of the ESOP Termination Date; (vi) all amendments required to be made to the ESOP under ERISA and the Code through the ESOP Termination Date; and (vii) any amendment required in connection with Section 6.18(b).

 

(b)      Prior to the Effective Time, the Bank shall have taken or caused to be taken the following actions: (i) in accordance with the ESOP and any ESOP Loan Documents in effect, the Bank shall make any contributions (including any interest payments on any ESOP Loan) required to be made to the ESOP for the plan year ending as of the ESOP Termination Date; (ii) repayment of the outstanding ESOP Loan by delivering a sufficient number of unallocated shares of Company Common Stock (with each remitted share to be valued equal to the Per Share Merger Consideration) in repayment of such outstanding ESOP Loan, and terminate any ESOP Loan Documentation (the “ESOP Loan Termination Documentation”); and (iii) cause the balance of the unallocated shares and any other unallocated assets remaining in the ESOP after repayment of the ESOP Loan to be allocated to the accounts of the ESOP participants in accordance in with the terms of the ESOP (and if the ESOP is silent on such allocation, in a manner compliant with ERISA and the Code, and subject to Purchaser’s prior approval).

 

52
 

 

Section 6.19    Terminated Arrangements. Prior to the Closing Date, the Company shall take (or cause to be taken) all actions necessary to terminate each plan, agreement, or arrangement set forth on set forth on Section 6.19 of the Schedules (each, a “Terminated Arrangement” and collectively, the “Terminated Arrangements”) as of the Effective Time, in each case in accordance with the requirements of Section 409A. The termination and liquidation of each Terminated Arrangement shall be effected in a manner consistent with the requirements of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or such other applicable exception as may be permitted under Section 409A. The form and substance of all board actions or documentation prepared in connection with the foregoing termination and liquidation of the Terminated Arrangements shall be subject to the prior review and approval of the Purchaser, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Subject to the provisions of this Section 6.19, following the termination of the Terminated Arrangements, all payments to be made in connection with such Terminated Arrangements (which amounts are set forth on Section 6.19 of the Schedules), shall be paid to each applicable individual in a single lump-sum cash payment on, or soon as administratively practicable following, the Closing Date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, with respect to each Terminated Arrangement identified on Section 6.19 of the Schedules as a “Release-Conditioned Arrangement,” payment shall be conditioned upon the applicable individual’s execution, delivery, and non-revocation of a termination and release of claims agreement in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit F.

Lear as a member of the Bank’s board of directors and (b) appoint one additional individual to the Bank’s board of directors, to be identified by the Purchaser, and to be consented to by the Company, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed, from the Bank’s current board of directors or from communities that the Bank serves, in each case effective immediately upon the Effective Time.

 

ARTICLE 8

COVENANTS OF ALL PARTIES 

 

Section 8.1      Regulatory Approvals. As soon as reasonably practicable following the Agreement Date, but no later than thirty (30) days after the Agreement Date, Purchaser shall make all appropriate public filings with Regulatory Authorities for approval of the Contemplated Transactions, including the preparation of an application or any amendment thereto or any other required statements or documents filed or to be filed by any party with: (a) the Federal Reserve; (b) the OCC; and (c) any other Person or Regulatory Authority pursuant to any applicable Legal Requirement (collectively, the “Regulatory Approvals”). Purchaser shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and pursue in good faith the Regulatory Approvals. In advance of any filing made under this Section 8.1, including without limitation, any supplemental filings, amendments or other related documents filed in response to any comments from any Regulatory Authorities or otherwise in connection with any filings contemplated by this Section 8.1, the Company and its counsel shall be provided, and have a reasonable opportunity to comment upon, all nonconfidential portions thereof and all such comments shall be considered in good faith. Promptly upon filing of any applications with the Regulatory Authorities, Purchaser shall provide the Company with a copy of the non-confidential portions of such filings, and Purchaser agrees promptly to advise the Company and its counsel of, and share with them, any material communication received by Purchaser or its counsel from any Regulatory Authorities with respect to the nonconfidential portions of such filings.

 

Section 8.2      Commercially Reasonable Efforts; Cooperation. Each of Purchaser and the Company agrees to exercise good faith and use its commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy the various covenants and conditions to Closing in this Agreement, and to consummate the Contemplated Transactions as promptly as possible. Neither Purchaser nor the Company will intentionally take or intentionally permit to be taken any action that would be a Breach of the terms or provisions of this Agreement. Between the Agreement Date and the Closing, Purchaser and the Company will, and will cause all of their respective Affiliates and Representatives to, cooperate with respect to all filings that any party is required by Legal Requirements to make in connection with the Contemplated Transactions.

 

54
 

 

Section 8.3      Director and Officer Indemnification.

 

(a)      From and after the Effective Time, Purchaser shall indemnify and hold harmless and shall advance expenses as incurred, in each case to the extent (subject to applicable Legal Requirements) such persons may entitled to such indemnification and advancement of expenses as of the Agreement Date by the Company pursuant to the Charter, the Bylaws and the governing or organizational documents of any Subsidiary of the Company, each present and former director, officer or employee of the Company and its Subsidiaries (in each case, when acting in such capacity) (collectively, the Company Indemnified Parties”) against any costs or expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees), judgments, fines, losses, damages, liabilities and other amounts incurred in connection with any threatened or actual claim, action, suit, proceeding or investigation, whether civil, criminal, administrative or investigative, whether arising before or after the Effective Time, arising out of the fact that such person is or was a director, officer or employee of the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and pertaining to matters existing or occurring at or prior to the Effective Time, including the Contemplated Transactions; provided, that in the case of advancement of expenses, the Company Indemnified Party to whom expenses are advanced provides an undertaking to repay such advances if it is ultimately determined that such Company Indemnified Party is not entitled to indemnification.

 

(b)      Prior to the Effective Time, the Company shall obtain an extension of its directors’ and officers’ liability insurance policy set forth on Section 8.3(b) of the Schedules (a complete and accurate copy of which have been heretofore made available to Purchaser) (the “Existing D&O Policy”) in respect of acts or omissions occurring at or prior to the Effective Time, covering each person currently covered by the Existing D&O Policy for a period of up to three (3) years after the Effective Time (the “Tail Policy”). The cost of the Tail Policy shall be borne by Purchaser; provided, however, that the parties shall not be required to pay in the aggregate more than 200% of the amount of the aggregate annual premium paid by the Company, as applicable, for the current policy term for such policy, which annual premium is set forth on Section 8.3(b) of the Schedules. It is understood and agreed that if the aggregate premiums for the coverage set forth in this Section 8.3(b) would exceed such 200% amount, the parties shall pay for the maximum available coverage as may be obtained by Purchaser for such 200% amount.

 

Section 8.4      Employees.

 

(a)      Purchaser or one of its Subsidiaries or Affiliates will for a period of one (1) year following the Closing, or, if earlier, until the date of termination of the Continuing Employee, provide each Continuing Employee with (i) annual base salary or wages that are no less than the annual base salary or wages, respectively, provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing, (ii) employee benefits (excluding any equity, equity-based and long-term incentive compensation, nonqualified deferred compensation, change in control, severance, retention, defined benefit arrangements, post-employment health and welfare benefits and employee stock ownership plan (the “Excluded Benefits”)) that are substantially similar in the aggregate to those benefits provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing.

 

55
 

 

(b)      From and after the Closing, Purchaser shall use commercially reasonable efforts to give or cause to be given to each Continuing Employee full credit for purposes of eligibility to participate and vesting, for purposes of vacation and paid time off, and for purpose of severance pay entitlement as provided under this Agreement (but not for any purposes of any Excluded Benefits or otherwise), under each employee benefit plan, program or arrangement established or maintained by Purchaser under which Continuing Employees are eligible to participate on or after the Closing to the same extent that such credit was recognized by the Company under comparable Benefit Plans, as applicable, immediately prior to the Closing; provided, however, that such credit shall not be provided to the extent that such credit would result in any duplication of benefits.

 

(c)      With respect to each welfare benefit plan, program or arrangement maintained, sponsored or contributed to by Purchaser after the Closing (collectively, the “Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plans”) in which any Continuing Employee or spouse or dependent thereof may be eligible to participate on or after the Closing, Purchaser shall use commercially reasonable efforts to (i) waive, or cause its Affiliates or insurance carrier to waive, all limitations as to preexisting conditions, actively-at-work requirements, exclusions and waiting periods, if any, with respect to participation and coverage requirements applicable to each Continuing Employee or spouse or dependent thereof, and any other restrictions that would prevent immediate or full participation by such Continued Employee or spouse or dependent thereof, under such Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plan, to the same extent satisfied or waived under a comparable Benefit Plan, as applicable, and (ii) provide or cause its Affiliates to provide full credit to each Continuing Employee or spouse or dependent thereof for any co-payments, deductibles, and out-of-pocket expenses paid by such Continuing Employee or spouse or dependent thereof under the comparable Benefit Plan, as applicable, during the relevant plan year up to and including the Closing as if such amounts had been paid under such Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plan.

 

(d)      Notwithstanding anything in this Section 8.4 to the contrary, nothing contained herein, whether express or implied, shall: (i) be treated as an establishment, amendment or other modification of any Benefit Plan or any Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plan, or any other employee benefit plan or arrangement of the Purchaser or its Affiliates or shall limit the right of Purchaser or any of its Affiliates to amend, terminate or otherwise modify any Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plan, Benefit Plan, or other employee benefit plan or arrangement of the Purchaser or its Affiliates following the Closing Date; or (ii) guarantee employment for any period of time for, or preclude the ability of Purchaser or its subsidiaries to terminate, any employee of the Company or its Subsidiaries, including the Bank, for any or no reason. The Company and Purchaser acknowledge and agree that all provisions contained in this Section 8.4 are included for their sole benefit, and that nothing in this Section 8.4, whether express or implied, shall create any third party beneficiary or other rights: (i) in any other Person, any participant in any Benefit Plan or Purchaser Welfare Benefit Plan, any other employee benefit plan or arrangement of the Purchaser or its Affiliates, or any dependent or beneficiary thereof; or (ii) to continued employment with Purchaser or any of its Affiliates, or to any particular term or condition of employment.

ARTICLE 9

CONDITIONS PRECEDENT TO OBLIGATIONS OF PURCHASER 

 

The obligations of Purchaser to consummate the Contemplated Transactions and to take the other actions required to be taken by Purchaser at the Closing are subject to the satisfaction, at or prior to the Closing, of each of the following conditions (any of which may be waived by Purchaser, in whole or in part):

 

Section 9.1      Accuracy of Representations and Warranties. All of the representations and warranties of the Company set forth in this Agreement shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date with the same force and effect as if all of such representations and warranties were made at the Closing; provided, however, that to the extent such representations and warranties expressly relate to an earlier date, such representations shall be true and correct in all material respects on and as of such earlier date; provided further, however, that to the extent any of the representations and warranties are subject in this Agreement to a standard of Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard, such representations and warranties shall be true and correct in all respects to the extent of the Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard set forth herein.

 

Section 9.2      Performance of the Company. The Company shall have performed or complied in all material respects with all of the covenants and obligations to be performed or complied with by it under the terms of this Agreement on or prior to the Closing Date; provided, however, that to the extent the performance and compliance with any covenants and obligations is subject in this Agreement to a standard of Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard, the Company shall have performed and complied in all respects with such covenants and obligations to the extent of the Knowledge, materiality, Material Adverse Effect or similar standard.

 

Section 9.3      Closing Deliveries. The Company shall have tendered for delivery all of the certificates, documents and other items listed in Section 2.8, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Purchaser.

 

Section 9.4      Absence of Material Adverse Effect. From the Agreement Date to the Closing, there shall have been no Material Adverse Effect with respect to the Company.

 

Section 9.5      Regulatory Approvals. (a) All Regulatory Approvals shall have been obtained and shall remain in full force and effect and all statutory waiting periods in respect thereof shall have expired or been terminated, and (b) no such Requisite Regulatory Approval shall have resulted in the imposition of any Burdensome Condition.

 

Section 9.6      Company Stockholder Approval. The Company Stockholder Approval shall have been obtained.

 

Section 9.7      Mortgage Division Disposition. The Mortgage Division Disposition shall have occurred.

 

Section 9.8      No Prohibition. The consummation of the Contemplated Transactions will not, directly or indirectly (with or without notice or lapse of time), materially contravene, or conflict with or result in a material violation of any Order against the Company or any of its Subsidiaries that has been proposed or issued by or before any Regulatory Authority after the Agreement Date.

ARTICLE 11

TERMINATION 

 

Section 11.1    Reasons for Termination and Abandonment. This Agreement may, by prompt written notice given to the other party prior to or at the Closing, be terminated:

 

(a)      By mutual written consent of the parties;

 

(b)      By Purchaser if the Company commits a Breach of this Agreement such that any of the conditions in ARTICLE 9 would not be satisfied, or satisfaction of such a condition would become impossible, as of the Closing, and such Breach is not cured, cannot be cured, or has not been waived in writing by Purchaser, on or before the Termination Date;

 

(c)      By the Company if Purchaser commits a Breach of this Agreement such that any of the conditions in ARTICLE 10 would not be satisfied, or satisfaction of such a condition would become impossible, as of the Closing, and such Breach is not cured, cannot be cured, or has not been waived in writing by the Company, on or before the Termination Date;

 

(d)      By Purchaser if the Company is in Breach of Section 6.5 or Section 6.6;

 

(e)      By the Company pursuant to Section 6.5; or

 

(f)      By Purchaser or the Company if the Closing has not occurred (other than through the failure of any party seeking to terminate this Agreement to comply with its obligations under this Agreement in all material respects) on or before the date that is nine (9) months after the Agreement Date, or such later date as the parties may agree in writing (the “Termination Date”); provided, that the party seeking to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 11.1(f) has used its commercially reasonable efforts to consummate the Contemplated Transactions prior to such date.

 

Section 11.2    Effect of Termination. Except as provided in Section 11.3 and Section 11.4, if this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Section 11.1, all further obligations of the parties under this Agreement will terminate, and there shall be no liability under this Agreement to or on the part of any party (or such party’s respective Representatives and Affiliates), and all rights and obligations of each party shall cease; provided, however, that nothing herein shall relieve any party from liability for fraud or the willful Breach of any of its representations and warranties or the Breach of any of its covenants or agreements set forth in this Agreement.

 

59
 

 

Section 11.3    Expenses. Except as otherwise expressly provided in Section 11.4, each party to this Agreement will bear its own respective expenses incurred in connection with the preparation, execution, and performance of this Agreement and the Contemplated Transactions, including all fees and expenses of Representatives.

 

Section 11.4    Termination Payments.

 

(a)      If this Agreement is terminated by Purchaser pursuant to Section 11.1(d) or by the Company pursuant to Section 11.1(e), then the Company shall pay to Purchaser, within two (2) Business Days after such termination, an amount equal to $3,000,000 (the “Company Termination Fee”) by wire transfer of immediately available funds to such account as Purchaser shall designate.

 

(b)      If, after the Agreement Date and prior to the termination of this Agreement, a bona fide Acquisition Proposal shall have been made known to the Company or any of its Subsidiaries or has been made directly to its stockholders generally or any Person shall have publicly announced (and not withdrawn) an Acquisition Proposal with respect to the Company or any of its Subsidiaries and (i) thereafter this Agreement is terminated by Purchaser pursuant to Section 11.1(b) and (ii) within twelve (12) months after such termination the Company or any of its Subsidiaries shall enter into a definitive written agreement with respect to such Acquisition Proposal, the Company shall pay to Purchaser the Company Termination Fee, payable in immediately available funds, within five (5) Business Days after the consummation of such definitive written agreement.

 

(c)      The sums payable pursuant to this Section 11.4 shall constitute liquidated damages and Purchaser’s receipt thereof shall be Purchaser’s sole and exclusive remedy under this Agreement for all Breaches of this Agreement by the Company set forth in this Section 11.4.

 

ARTICLE 12

MISCELLANEOUS 

 

Section 12.1    Governing Law. All questions concerning the construction, validity and interpretation of this Agreement, and the performance of the obligations imposed by this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of Illinois applicable to Contracts made and wholly to be performed in such state without regard to conflicts of laws.

Each party hereby irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Illinois solely in respect of the interpretation and enforcement of the provisions of this Agreement and of the documents referred to in this Agreement, and in respect of the Contemplated Transactions, and hereby waives, and agrees not to assert, as a defense in any action, suit or Proceeding for the interpretation or enforcement hereof or of any such document, that it is not subject thereto or that such action, suit or Proceeding may not be brought or is not maintainable in said court or that the venue thereof may not be appropriate or that this Agreement or any such document may not be enforced in or by such court, and the parties hereto irrevocably agree that all claims with respect to such action or Proceeding shall be heard and determined in such court. The parties hereby consent to and grant any such court jurisdiction over the Person of such parties and agree that mailing of process or other papers in connection with any such action or Proceeding in the manner provided under Section 12.8 or in such other manner as may be permitted by Legal Requirements shall be valid and sufficient service thereof. EACH PARTY ACKNOWLEDGES AND AGREES THAT ANY CONTROVERSY WHICH MAY ARISE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IS LIKELY TO INVOLVE COMPLICATED AND DIFFICULT ISSUES, AND THEREFORE EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT SUCH PARTY MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN RESPECT OF ANY LITIGATION DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE CONTEMPLATED TRANSACTIONS. Section 12.3    Assignments, Successors and No Third Party Rights. No party may assign any of its rights under this Agreement to any other Person without the prior written consent of the other parties, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Subject to the preceding sentence, this Agreement and every representation, warranty, covenant, agreement and provision hereof shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Nothing expressed or referred to in this Agreement will be construed to give any Person other than the parties to this Agreement any legal or equitable right, remedy or claim under or with respect to this Agreement or any provision of this Agreement. This Agreement and all of its provisions and conditions are for the sole and exclusive benefit of the parties to this Agreement and their successors and assigns.

 

Section 12.4    Waiver. The rights and remedies of the parties to this Agreement are cumulative and not alternative. Neither the failure nor any delay by any party in exercising any right, power or privilege under this Agreement or the documents referred to in this Agreement will operate as a waiver of such right, power or privilege, and no single or partial exercise of any such right, power or privilege will preclude any other or further exercise of such right, power or privilege or the exercise of any other right, power or privilege. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law: (a) no claim or right arising out of this Agreement or the documents referred to in this Agreement can be discharged by one party, in whole or in part, by a waiver or renunciation of the claim or right unless in writing signed by the other parties; (b) no waiver that may be given by a party will be applicable except in the specific instance for which it is given; and (c) no notice to or demand on one party will be deemed to be a waiver of any obligation of such party or of the right of the party giving such notice or demand to take further action without notice or demand as provided in this Agreement or the documents referred to in this Agreement.

 

Section 12.5    Modification. This Agreement may only be amended by a written agreement executed by each of the parties hereto.

Section 12.6    Publicity. Prior to the Closing and except as required by any applicable Legal Requirements, the parties hereto will consult with each other before issuing any press releases or otherwise making any public statements with respect to this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions and shall not issue any such press release or make any such public statement without the prior consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. Section 12.7    Confidentiality. Between the Agreement Date and the Closing, each of Purchaser and the Company will maintain in confidence, and will cause their Affiliates and Representatives to maintain in confidence, and not use for any purpose, other than evaluating the Contemplated Transaction, or to the detriment of the other party any written, oral or other information obtained in confidence from the other party in connection with this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions, unless: (a) such information is already known to or becomes known to such party or to others not bound by a duty of confidentiality or such information becomes publicly available through no fault of such party; (b) the use of such information is necessary or appropriate in making any filing or obtaining any consent or approval required for the consummation of the Contemplated Transactions; or (c) the furnishing or use of such information is required by or necessary in connection with any Proceedings.
